# Opcode coverage and version lifecycle

<!-- Generated by HermesProxy.Tests/World/Dispatch/OpcodeCoverageReportTests.cs.
     Do not edit by hand: the test rewrites this file and fails when it is stale. -->

Two independent axes, and conflating them is the easiest mistake to make here:

- **Modern / client axis** — `ModernVersion`, the retail or Classic client talking to the
  proxy. `[HandlesCmsg]` and most `[PacketCodec]` ranges are measured against it.
- **Legacy / server axis** — `LegacyVersion`, the emulator the proxy talks to.
  `[HandlesSmsg]` ranges are measured against it.

A build number is only comparable within its own branch (`ClientBranch`): the Classic-line
`V3_4_3_54261` is 54261 while the original-line `V4_3_4_15595` is 15595, so an ordered
comparison across branches is meaningless. `VersionChecker.AssertComparableBranch` enforces
that at runtime.

## 1. Dispatch coverage per build

`defined` is how many opcodes of that direction the build's generated table maps at all.
`handled` is how many of those have a handler whose range covers the build. `gap` is the
remainder — opcodes the client can send, or the server can send us, that fall through to a
"No handler for opcode" log line. A gap is not automatically a bug: much of it is traffic
the proxy has no reason to translate.

|---|---:|---:|---:|

| `V2_5_3_41750` | 694 | 381 | 313 |
| `V3_4_3_54261` | 449 | 381 | 68 |

the dispatch table is constructed, not per packet. All of these are on the legacy axis;
there are no ranged `[HandlesCmsg]` sites yet, which is itself the finding: every per-build
difference on the modern side currently hides inside a handler body instead (see section 4).

## 4. Exact-equality version checks — the new-client work list

`ModernVersion.Build == ClientVersionBuild.X` (or `!=`) inside a method body. These are the
sites that do **not** carry forward: a build the code has never seen fails the equality and
takes the `else`, which is generally the oldest supported layout — the opposite of what a
newer client wants, and silent when wrong.

Converting one to a range (`AddedInVersion`, or a second `[PacketCodec]`) makes it inherit
correctly by default. They cannot be swept mechanically: some genuinely mean "this build
only" — a quirk a later client fixed — and widening those would propagate a bug forward.
Each needs a judgement call against the client or WowPacketParser.

Counts per file rather than line numbers, so unrelated edits do not churn this file.

213 sites across 55 files.
